name: Shopify
title: Shopify SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Shopify: 16 of 27 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in — but it needs a /proxy/shopify/ route the storefront does not ship.
lede: The Shopify connector is scored out of 27, not 43: several storefront services have no equivalent in the Shopify API surface it targets. Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired — but every request goes through a proxy route you have to write.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired, but it does not run as installed. The connector sends every request to a `/proxy/shopify/` route on the storefront’s own server, with the Shopify request path encoded in it, and Svelte Commerce ships no such route — only one for Bagisto. Until you write it, nothing reaches Shopify.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Shopify store

quickStartNote: The guide removes only `@misiki/litekart-connector`. A fresh clone’s `package.json` also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector`, and with two connectors installed and neither of them Litekart’s, the build stops and asks for `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR` — so this removes both. This starts the storefront, but read the limitations: the connector needs a `/proxy/shopify/` route that the storefront does not ship.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHOPIFY_API_URL
env.note: Your store’s `myshopify.com` domain. Shopify is keyed on a domain rather than a URL, so any `https://` you include is stripped. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: The guide’s example is an Admin API access token, `shpat_…`. Handed to the connector at boot — and to every visitor’s browser; see the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHOPIFY_STOREFRONT_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: A Storefront API access token, handed over the same way.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHOPIFY_PROXY_URL
env.note: Read at boot and stored by the connector, for stores fronted by a proxy. In 1.1.0 and 1.1.1 the request path is fixed at `/proxy/shopify/`, so setting it changes nothing yet.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/shopify-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: Shopify is one of four backends `init.ts` configures by hand rather than by forwarding every `PUBLIC_SHOPIFY_*` variable: it passes the domain, the two tokens and the proxy URL to `setShopifyCredentials`, in that order.
backendSettings: Create the access tokens in Shopify: an Admin API token (the guide’s `shpat_…`) and a Storefront API token.

Write a server route at `/proxy/shopify/[...path]` in the storefront. The connector base32-encodes the Shopify request path into the route’s path and says which API it wants in an `X-Shopify-Api-Type` header — `admin` or `storefront` — but attaches no token itself; the route has to add the right one and forward the request. The storefront’s `/proxy/bagisto/` route is the nearest pattern to copy.
howItWorks: Shopify is keyed on a store domain rather than a URL. At boot, `init.ts` strips any `https://` from `PUBLIC_SHOPIFY_API_URL` and passes the domain, the Admin and Storefront tokens and the proxy URL to the connector’s `setShopifyCredentials`, in both the server and the client hook.

The connector sends every call — Admin API or Storefront API — to `/proxy/shopify/<base32-encoded path>` on the storefront’s own origin, marked `X-Shopify-Api-Type: admin` or `storefront`. It never sends a token itself: the proxy is expected to. Svelte Commerce ships a proxy route of this kind for Bagisto, not for Shopify.
limitations: Nothing reaches Shopify until you add a `/proxy/shopify/` server route: the connector sends every request there, and the storefront does not ship one.
Scored out of 27 rather than 43: several storefront services have no equivalent in the Shopify API surface this connector targets.

The guide puts an Admin API token (`shpat_…`) in `PUBLIC_SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN`. SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser, so every visitor could read it and call Shopify’s Admin API with it. A server route is the place for that token, not a `PUBLIC_` variable.

troubleshooting.problem: Every call fails with a 404 on `/proxy/shopify/…`
troubleshooting.fix: The storefront has no Shopify proxy route. Add a server route at `/proxy/shopify/[...path]` that decodes the base32 path, adds the Admin or Storefront token according to `X-Shopify-Api-Type`, and forwards the request to Shopify.

faq.q: Can I run a Shopify store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Not as installed. Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired, but the connector sends every request to a `/proxy/shopify/` route on the storefront’s server, and Svelte Commerce does not ship one. Writing that route — and keeping the Admin token in it, out of `PUBLIC_` variables — is the missing step.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Shopify?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/shopify-connector`, set `PUBLIC_SHOPIFY_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Why is Shopify scored out of 27 instead of 43?
faq.a: Several of the storefront’s 43 services have no equivalent in the Shopify API surface the connector targets, so they are not counted. Of the 27 that are, 16 are wired; reviews, wishlist, vendors, CMS pages, profile and countries are the gaps.

api.surface: The connector calls Shopify’s Storefront GraphQL API as `POST /graphql.json` for the catalogue, cart, checkout and customer, and a few Admin REST paths such as `/shop.json`, `/customers/{id}.json` and `/price_rules.json`, every one of them through the storefront’s `/proxy/shopify/` route.
api.auth: The connector attaches no store token itself and leaves that to the proxy route; a shopper signs in with the Storefront `mutation customerAccessTokenCreate`, the returned access token is kept in `localStorage` under `customerAccessToken`, and it is sent as the `customerAccessToken` GraphQL variable rather than as a header.

calls.what: `query getCart` for `cost` and `deliveryGroups(first: 1)` delivery options; `mutation cartAttributesUpdate` (with `cartNoteUpdate` for cash on delivery) to read the cart’s `checkoutUrl`

rules: The request paths carry no API version: Storefront calls go to `/graphql.json` and Admin calls to paths such as `/shop.json`, and the `/admin/api/2026-01` prefix defined in the base service appears only in a commented-out line.

Every payment method the storefront offers, cash on delivery, Razorpay, PhonePe, PayPal and Stripe, sets a `return_url` cart attribute and hands back the cart’s `checkoutUrl`, so the shopper pays on Shopify’s own checkout; cash on delivery also writes a cart note and redirects the browser itself.

The product list builds a Shopify search string from `title:`, `tag:`, `vendor:` and `collection:` terms, and reports the number of products it got back as the count, because the query asks for no total.

A stored cart id is used only if it contains `gid://shopify/Cart/`; anything else, or a cart Shopify no longer returns, makes the connector create a new cart, and the id is saved in `localStorage` as both `shopify_cart_id` and `cart_id`.
Order history needs the signed-in shopper’s token: without `customerAccessToken` in `localStorage` the order list returns empty without making a request.
